tasks.title: Rebase custom-next onto v0.10.0 and resolve the 13 conflicting files
tasks.detail:
Goal: land all eight fork commits on top of upstream v0.10.0 with fork behaviour preserved.
Files: the list above are the files git reports as conflicted or that the fork patches touch; `package-lock.json` is regenerated by npm in the next task and must not be hand-edited.
Contract: this hop moves pi from 0.87.1 to 1.0.0 (a major bump), Next stays 16.3.6, and upstream adds its first MCP/codemode groundwork. Resolution policy per file:
- AGENTS.md: keep the whole upstream text, then keep the fork-only sections (in-place file editing, pinned sessions, package web panels, sudo password prompt, extension run mode) and delete fork sections describing code that upstream replaced.
- README.md: keep the fork attribution block at the top (unofficial fork, upstream link, MIT), take upstream body verbatim.
- package.json: take upstream dependencies/scripts/version, then re-add the fork-only dependencies (codemirror packages added by the file editor commit). Keep `version` equal to the upstream release being rebased onto.
- lib/rpc-manager.ts: take upstream wholesale, then re-apply the three fork patches: (a) `PI_WEB_EXTENSION_MODE` chooses the advertised `ctx.mode`, (b) `onTerminalInput` is omitted instead of a no-op listener, (c) percentage overlay widths map to a real column count. If the SDK changed the surrounding API, port the intent, not the old code.
- app/api/files/[...path]/route.ts: keep upstream GET/POST (upload) and add the fork PUT save handler plus the `revision` field in the text read response.
- lib/api-types.ts, hooks/useAgentSession.ts, components/AppShell.tsx, components/ChatWindow.tsx: take upstream, then re-apply fork-only additions (pinned session ids in the session list payload, file-tab edit/dirty state, plugin panel tab kind).
- lib/i18n/messages/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts: union — keep every upstream key, then add fork keys; no key may be dropped from any locale.
Steps:
1. cd /home/ljosalfar-server/Documents/pi-web-upstream; `git rebase --onto v0.10.0 0876cf4` (0876cf4 is the v0.9.3 merge base recorded in this plan).
2. Resolve conflicts commit by commit, applying the policy above; `git add` then `git rebase --continue`.
3. When the rebase reports success, run `git log --oneline v0.10.0..HEAD` and confirm exactly the eight fork commits remain.
Verify: `git status` is clean, `git rev-list --count v0.10.0..HEAD` is 8, and `git diff v0.10.0..HEAD --stat` only lists fork-owned files.
Done when: the rebase finished with fork behaviour preserved and no conflict markers anywhere (`git grep -n '^<<<<<<<'` prints nothing).

tasks.title: Install pi 1.0.0, fix SDK drift, and tag the verified hop
tasks.detail:
Goal: prove the v0.10.0 hop compiles and passes the unit suites against pi 1.0.0, fixing only the drift the rebase exposed.
Files: `package-lock.json` is regenerated by npm; SDK-facing type fixes belong in lib/rpc-manager.ts and lib/pi-types.ts; unrelated files must not be touched.
Contract: no new dependency may be added beyond what the fork already declared; a type fix must not change runtime behaviour.
Steps:
1. `npm install` in the worktree so node_modules matches the rebased package.json (pi 1.0.0).
2. `node_modules/.bin/tsc --noEmit`.
3. Fix each reported error at its source (SDK signature changes, removed helpers, renamed fields). Re-run until exit 0. Do not silence errors with `any` casts that hide a real API change.
4. `npm test` and fix genuine regressions; a test whose expectation upstream changed is updated to the upstream contract.
5. `git commit` the fixes, then `git tag fork-next-v0.10.0`.
Verify: tsc exit 0, `npm test` with zero failing tests, tag `fork-next-v0.10.0` present on HEAD.
Done when: the hop is green and tagged, with the install/typecheck/test output recorded in progress.
